thread:
alex: Quick design thought — proposing a hierarchical per-org ratecap model. org-level RPM/TPM + per-key concurrency caps + burst credits. On overload fallbacks: 1) soft scale, 2) route to cheaper model, 3) reject. Thoughts?

maria: prefer explicit fallback priorities in routing policy. reject only as last resort :+1:

jeff: need short burst credits so noisy startups don't get nuked. also how does TPM work for streaming/chat?

linda: telemetry question — need per-org metrics: throttles_by_reason, fallback_count, avg_latency_post_fallback. dashboards?

alex: yeah dash needs a per-org view with timeline. suggested metric names: org.rate_limit.exceeded, org.concurrent.blocked, org.fallback.model_switch

zach: small infra q: enforce concurrency at the edge or at the serving pool? edge enforcement faster but can be stale across edges.

maria: prefer enforcement at edge for immediate rejection, but validate at runtime for safety (idempotent decrement on completion). Router today has token buckets for RPM.

alex: current state: router enforces RPM via token bucket. Concurrency enforced at serving only. Proposal: add lightweight concurrency counters in router using Redis INCR/DECR with short TTL.

jeff: Redis contention risk — shard by org+route and use local caching for tiny bursts. recommend per-shard capacity limits.

linda: dashboard ops: show throttled_requests, blocked_concurrency, burst_credit_balance. also per-model fallback rates and time-to-recover.

alex: sample policy snippet for proto: 
```
policy:
  - scope: org
    rpm: 30000
    tpm: 180000
    concurrency: 200
    burst_credits: 500
  - fallback:
      - model: gptx-medium
        when: cpu_usage > 80%
      - model: gptx-small
        when: rps > threshold
```

maria: this looks good. Need to decide calculation window for RPM/TPM (sliding vs fixed window). Sliding is smoother but heavier to compute.

zach: sliding with exponential decay approximates sliding window, same op count as fixed if we use leaky-bucket per org. good tradeoff.

jeff: add per-org tiers: free-tier lower concurrency and smaller burst credits, enterprise can have burst carryover. Also need billing hooks when we auto-scale.

alex: rollout plan: 1) logging-only mode for 2w, 2) soft-throttle (warn + 429 on 10% sampling) for 1w, 3) strict enforce. We'll include a kill-switch per-org.

linda: expose per-org usage in console + API so customers can request temporary burst increases. add audit log entries for approvals.

maria: +1 on API. Also keep metric cardinality low — tag by org+model+route only, avoid extra labels.

bot-deploy: deploy scheduled: feature/ratecaps -> staging at 2025-07-12T03:00Z

jeff: streaming edge-case: long-running streams hold concurrency slots. option: streaming_weight < 1 so streams count for fewer slots. will need fairness tests.

alex: propose streaming_weight=0.5 default; will add to policy schema as optional. Complex but helps throughput.

maria: add tests for weighted streaming and preflight checks for starving short requests.

alex: action items:
- jeff: prototype router Redis counters (due 1w)
- linda: dashboard mockups + metric contracts (due 2w)
- maria: policy schema PR + docs (due 3d)
- zach: telemetry cardinality and storage cost check (due 1w)

maria: i'll start the policy PR today :tada:

alex: thanks all :rocket:
